messages.body_plain:
Hi Yang,
I got this to work with the SAF file as you described. Unfortunately the results do not make sense. Again, I wanted to know how many reads map to a region on human chromosome 11 (47,371,468 bp to 47,441,229 bp). Using featureCounts with the SAF file as you described I obtained a read count for 477 individuals. Summing the read counts of the individuals gave a total of 439,789 reads. The GTF file (Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.96.gtf) has 4 meta-features associated with this region, 3 are contained in the region and one overlaps with the region. Below are the gene-ids and start and end positions of these features:
ENSG00000066336  47354860 47378576
ENSG00000255197  47383148 47409190
ENSG00000264583  47400970 47401042
ENSG00000165915  47407132 47416496

I obtained read counts for all features using featureCounts with the GTF file and summed the read counts for each feature across the 477 individuals:
ENSG00000066336: 3,133,973
ENSG00000255197:   685,739
ENSG00000264583:       508
ENSG00000165915:   201,686

Ignoring the first feature which only partially overlaps the region, the read counts of the remaining 3 features (685739+508+201686) add up to a count that is larger than the count for the region (439789).
Do you have any idea what is going wrong here?

Thanks much again, Ina

messages.body_plain:
It appeared that you did strand-specific read assignment in both runs (strandSpecific = 2 : the reads are assigned to the genes that are on the opposite strand). Namely, when you assign reads to the region of interest defined in the SAF file, you only included the reads that were mapped to the negative strand (because the region of interest is on the positive strand). However, some of your four genes in the GTF file are on the positive strand but some are on negative strand, hence the set of reads assigned to the four genes is different to the set of reads assigned to the interest region. For example,  ENSG00000255197 is on negative strand, hence only the reads that are mapped to the positive strand are assigned to this gene.

Because you want to do strand-specific read assignment, and the four genes are on different strands, what is the number of reads you want to have in the region of interest? If you just want to have the total read number mapped to the region of interest disregarding their strands, you can remove the "strandSpecific" option from your first run (with SAF), but it will still be inconstant to your gene-level read assignment (with GTF file).

Hi again, Yiang,
I have counted reads in several regions using the unstranded option. The results are very encouraging and therefore we decided to explore these regions further.
We would like to see the distribution of reads across a region, separately for the + and - strands. I have partitioned a region into 100 bp intervals, have created a SAF file containing the interval boundaries, and am counting reads for these intervals, in one run by specifying the + strand for each interval in the SAF file and in a separate run by specifying the - strand for each interval in the SAF file. I am running featureCounts in both cases with the option strandSpecific=2 (reversely stranded) as this is Illumina data. Using strandSpecific=2 both for counting on the + and the - strand is correct, right? The counting is taking a very long time on the - strand.
Thanks, Ina

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ina,

If my understanding is correct, you created two SAF files: one with all 100-bp buckets on the positive strand and the other with all buckets on the negative strand, then you use strandSpecific=2 to assign reads to either of these SAF files.

If you use strandSpecific=2, you can have strand-specific counting results (only reads mapped to the opposite strand of the buckets are counted). It is less straightforward than using strandSpecific=1 (counting reads that are mapped to the same strand of the buckets) but you can still work out the correct counts to either strands.

I'm not sure why it takes a very long time on the negative strand -- the speed should be similar on both strands, and it should be very fast (if you use like 16 threads). Does the counting result to the negative strand make sense?

Cheers,
Yang
